title: Library of Alexandria
summary: A scalable, self-documenting library of knowledge — browse a tree of topics, highlight any term for an inline definition, and explore interactive lessons.

children.title: Calculus
children.summary: A template topic: the mathematics of continuous change, from limits and derivatives to integrals.

children.title: Limits
children.summary: The foundational idea of approaching a value, underpinning both derivatives and integrals.

children.title: Derivatives
children.summary: Instantaneous rates of change and the slope of a curve at a point.

children.title: Integrals
children.summary: Accumulation and area under a curve — the inverse of differentiation.

children.title: Game Theory
children.summary: A template topic: the study of strategic decision-making among rational agents.

children.title: Nash Equilibrium
children.summary: A strategy profile where no player can gain by unilaterally changing their own strategy.

children.title: Dominant Strategies
children.summary: Strategies that yield a better outcome for a player regardless of what the others do.

children.title: Prisoner's Dilemma
children.summary: The classic game showing why two rational agents may fail to cooperate even when it serves them both.

children.title: Computational Cortical Columns
children.summary: A learning path from the biology of the neocortical column to building one in spiking neurons: neuron models, plasticity, HTM, the Thousand Brains Theory, other column models, and a practical build roadmap.

children.title: 1. Biology of the Neocortex
children.summary: What a cortical column is made of: layers, minicolumns, cell types, thalamic loops, and Mountcastle's hypothesis.

children.title: Cortical Layers L1–L6
children.summary: The six-layer laminar structure, what each layer receives and sends, and why it matters for models.

children.title: Minicolumns and Columns
children.summary: Minicolumns, macrocolumns and barrels: the repeated vertical units of cortex and how big they really are.

children.title: Cell Types
children.summary: Excitatory pyramidal and spiny stellate cells, and the PV, SST and VIP inhibitory interneuron classes.

children.title: Thalamocortical Loops
children.summary: Core and matrix thalamus, driver vs modulator inputs, and the cortex–thalamus–cortex loop.

children.title: Mountcastle's Hypothesis
children.summary: The idea that every cortical region runs the same algorithm — evidence, limits, and why it motivates column models.

children.title: 2. Spiking Neuron Models
children.summary: The single-neuron building blocks: integrate-and-fire, Izhikevich, Hodgkin–Huxley, synapses and active dendrites.

children.title: Leaky Integrate-and-Fire
children.summary: The workhorse point-neuron model: intuition, equation, f–I curve, and an interactive simulation.

children.title: Izhikevich Model
children.summary: A two-variable model that reproduces cortical firing patterns (regular spiking, bursting, fast spiking) cheaply.

children.title: Hodgkin–Huxley Overview
children.summary: The biophysical conductance model behind the action potential, and when you need it.

children.title: Synapse Models
children.summary: Current- vs conductance-based synapses, exponential kernels, delays, and NMDA/AMPA/GABA receptors.

children.title: Dendrites and Active Dendrites
children.summary: Dendritic compartments, NMDA spikes, and why distal dendrites let a neuron recognise many patterns and predict.

children.title: 3. Plasticity and Learning
children.summary: How columns learn without labels: Hebbian rules, STDP, homeostasis, inhibition and k-winners-take-all, and sparse distributed representations.

children.title: Hebbian Learning
children.summary: "Cells that fire together wire together": Hebb's postulate, Oja's rule, BCM, and why plain Hebb is unstable.

children.title: Spike-Timing-Dependent Plasticity
children.summary: Pair-based STDP, its learning window, traces for online implementation, and an interactive explorer.

children.title: Homeostatic Plasticity
children.summary: Synaptic scaling, adaptive thresholds, intrinsic plasticity, and boosting — keeping activity in a useful range.

children.title: Inhibition and k-Winners-Take-All
children.summary: How inhibitory interneurons enforce competition and sparsity, from E/I balance to the k-WTA abstraction.

children.title: Sparse Distributed Representations
children.summary: The math of SDRs: capacity, overlap, robustness to noise, unions, and false-match probabilities.

children.title: 4. Hierarchical Temporal Memory
children.summary: Numenta's HTM: the HTM neuron, the spatial pooler, temporal memory, and sequence prediction with distal dendrites.

children.title: The HTM Neuron
children.summary: Proximal, basal and apical zones; dendritic segments as coincidence detectors; the predictive state.

children.title: Spatial Pooler
children.summary: Turning encoder output into stable SDRs with competitive Hebbian learning, inhibition and boosting.

children.title: Temporal Memory
children.summary: Minicolumns of cells, bursting vs predicted activation, and high-order sequence learning on distal segments.

children.title: Sequence Prediction and Anomaly Detection
children.summary: Branching sequences, multiple simultaneous predictions, anomaly scores, and continuous online learning.

children.title: 5. The Thousand Brains Theory
children.summary: Every column learns complete models of objects in reference frames and columns vote to reach consensus.

children.title: Reference Frames
children.summary: Why location is central: objects modelled as features at locations in object-centric reference frames.

children.title: Grid and Displacement Cells
children.summary: Grid cells, path integration, and how cortical grid-like cells could encode locations and displacements.

children.title: Sensorimotor Object Recognition
children.summary: Recognising objects by moving sensors over them: feature-location pairs and narrowing hypotheses.

children.title: Voting Between Columns
children.summary: Long-range lateral connections let many columns reach consensus fast — with an interactive voting demo.

children.title: Monty and the Thousand Brains Project
children.summary: The open-source sensorimotor learning system: learning modules, sensor modules, and the Cortical Messaging Protocol.

children.title: 6. Other Column Models
children.summary: Alternative views of what a column computes and how it has been simulated.

children.title: Canonical Microcircuit
children.summary: Douglas and Martin's canonical circuit: recurrent excitation, amplification and the layer-to-layer flow.

children.title: Predictive Coding
children.summary: Rao and Ballard's prediction-error hierarchy and its proposed laminar mapping in the cortical column.

children.title: Potjans–Diesmann Microcircuit
children.summary: The 2014 full-density spiking model of 1 mm² of cortex with eight populations — a standard benchmark.

children.title: Blue Brain and Detailed Reconstruction
children.summary: Markram et al.'s biophysically detailed digital reconstruction of a neocortical microcircuit.

children.title: 7. Building an SNN Column
children.summary: From reading to running: simulators, neuromorphic hardware, encoders, evaluation, a step-by-step roadmap and common pitfalls.

children.title: Simulators and Frameworks
children.summary: Brian2, NEST, Nengo, Norse, snnTorch, Lava and friends — what each is good for, with code.

children.title: Neuromorphic Hardware
children.summary: Loihi, SpiNNaker, TrueNorth, BrainScaleS and FPGAs: mapping a column onto event-driven silicon.

children.title: Encoding Schemes
children.summary: Rate, latency, population and delta coding, and HTM-style scalar and grid-cell encoders that produce SDRs.

children.title: Evaluating a Column
children.summary: Biological plausibility checks, representation metrics, prediction and anomaly benchmarks, and object recognition.

children.title: Step-by-Step Roadmap
children.summary: A staged plan from one LIF neuron to a multi-column sensorimotor system, with checks at each stage.

children.title: Common Pitfalls
children.summary: Runaway excitation, silent networks, dead units, time-step artefacts, and other mistakes that cost weeks.

children.title: 8. Key Papers and Reading List
children.summary: Annotated citations: neuroscience of the column, neuron and plasticity models, HTM and Thousand Brains, simulators and hardware.
